subject: Service downtime summary and verification playbook
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Ryan Patel <ryan.patel@corebank.com>, Elena Gomez <elena.gomez@corebank.com>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-07-31T02:14:00Z
Subject: Brief service disruption — what we know right now

Hi Ryan / Elena —

Thank you for your patience this morning. I wanted to send a concise note from Redwood with what we can confirm so far about the disruption your traffic experienced between 01:05–01:42 UTC today. We know this hit your production inference endpoint and some requests timed out or returned 503.

Quick summary (high level):
- Impact window: ~01:05:12 UTC — 01:42:08 UTC.
- Affected routes: /v1/predict (model: redwood-llama-13b-v1, customer pinned).
- User impact: ~18% of requests returned errors or timed out; the remainder were served with elevated latency.

What we are doing now:
- Engineering is investigating and collecting service-level traces and kernel logs.
- We will produce a short timeline and a proposed remediation plan by end of next business day.
- We will provide a verification playbook so you can validate recovery in your environment.

Please let me know if you need us to pause any non-critical traffic for you while we do deeper validation. I will follow up with a full timeline and root cause analysis once we complete the internal review.

Apologies again for the disruption — we know these interruptions are costly and we'll treat this as urgent.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment: timeline_extracted.csv (short event list)
From: Ryan Patel <ryan.patel@corebank.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Gomez <elena.gomez@corebank.com>
Date: 2027-07-31T03:07:00Z
Subject: Re: Brief service disruption — what we know right now

Naomi —

Thanks for the quick note. Two immediate asks from our side:
1) Did any inference outputs breach PII handling rules (we log no customer-sensitive data but want confirmation).
2) ETA for the remediation plan and whether we should move traffic to the dedicated fallback pool you mentioned during onboarding.

Also tagging our security lead Elena in case you need to loop in any evidence for audit.

Ryan
Director, Platform Engineering — CoreBank

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Ryan Patel <ryan.patel@corebank.com>, Elena Gomez <elena.gomez@corebank.com>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-08-01T14:05:00Z
Subject: Follow-up: preliminary findings, impact scope, and attached artifacts

Hi Ryan / Elena —

Quick follow-up with preliminary findings from the engineering investigation. I've included the key facts first, then attachments and next steps.

Preliminary technical summary (high level):
- Root cause (short): an unexpected kernel mismatch combined with a concurrent autoscaler spike caused a partial eviction of some model KV caches on the inference nodes. When the cache warmup occurred under load we saw request queueing and then transient 503s as worker threads failed health checks.
- Why this affected you: your customer route was pinned to a mixed-capacity pool where we had a rolling kernel rollout earlier that day; the timing aligned with a traffic surge from your scheduled batch jobs.
- No evidence of data exfiltration or PII exposure found in our traces or audit logs; we will provide signed evidence snapshot for your auditors.

Attached artifacts (for your review):
- timeline_extracted.csv — low-level event timestamps we pulled from telemetry (attached).
- mitigation-action-register.xlsx — actions engineering is tracking and owners.

Planned remediation and verification playbook (summary):
1) Immediate: pin your route to the dedicated fallback pool (no config change required from you; we can perform live switch at a scheduled time).
2) Short term (1–2 weeks): revert the kernel rollout on the affected node group, add a guarded staggered rollout policy, and add extra cache warmup steps in the runtime.
3) Medium term (4–8 weeks): introduce proactive cache pre-warming on scale events and an autoscaler threshold refinement to avoid simultaneous worker restarts.
4) Verification playbook: we'll share a PDF checklist you can run with your SREs to validate the fix end-to-end (latency, error-rate, trace correlation).

If you'd like us to make the fallback pool switch tonight at 22:00 local (US/Eastern) please confirm and we'll schedule a maintenance window with a 15-minute blackout.

Next deliverables: final root cause analysis document, copy of the signed telemetry snapshot for auditors, and the verification playbook PDF (sent now).

Sincerely,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: mitigation-action-register.xlsx
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Ryan Patel <ryan.patel@corebank.com>, Elena Gomez <elena.gomez@corebank.com>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, alex_martinez@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-08-01T17:22:00Z
Subject: Final: downtime summary + verification playbook (action items & timelines)

Hi Ryan / Elena —

Thanks again for working with us as we closed the investigation. Attached is the verification playbook (downtime_verification_playbook.pdf) and the consolidated mitigation register. Below is a compact customer-facing RCA and a straightforward checklist you can run with your SREs.

Customer-facing RCA (concise):
- Event: transient service degradation and partial 503s affecting pinned customer routes.
- Cause: incompatible kernel rollout combined with a scale-up activity that caused partial KV cache eviction; the cache warmup under load led to thread health failures and temporary request rejections.
- Impact: ~18% error rate during 01:05–01:42 UTC, no data leakage, persisted traces show no PII in transit logs.

Committed remediation (owner / timeline):
- Revert kernel rollout on affected node group — Owner: infra-release (jonas_weber) — Complete by: 2027-08-02 23:59 UTC.
- Implement staggered rollout policy for kernels — Owner: infra-release — Complete by: 2027-08-09.
- Autoscaler threshold tuning to prevent concurrent worker restarts — Owner: marissa_cole — Complete by: 2027-08-06.
- Cache pre-warm on scale events (runtime change) — Owner: alex_martinez — Planned for 2027-08-28.

Verification checklist (for your SRE team):
1) Confirm route is pinned to fallback pool and monitor 5-minute rolling error rate for 24 hours.
2) Run the supplied synthetic test (steps in PDF) with traffic ramp to 2x baseline while observing latency P95 and error rate.
3) Validate trace correlation keys for requests during test — we will provide a short script to fetch traces for the window.
4) Confirm no PII appears in request/response logs for the synthetic tests.

Attachments: downtime_verification_playbook.pdf, mitigation-action-register.xlsx

We will update the Jira ticket INF-9832 with verification artifacts and a signed telemetry snapshot for your compliance team once you confirm the verification window. If you want, we can run the synthetic test jointly and share the screen to walk through the signals.

Apologies again for the outage and thank you for the partnership in validating our changes.

Best regards,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
